item.title: MicroShader v4.1.0
item.description: ### Added New **Capture GIF** action for the live viewport, with three built-in size/duration presets, animated and looping. The **Twigl Export** tab (mode, ES 3.00, MRT, backbuffer, sound) now keeps its own state per document, the same way the golfing profile already did. New **Import twigl shader** button: pastes twigl.app-formatted code and converts it back into a normal, editable shader. The "Copy for twigl.app" button (and the matching command-palette action) now shows a confirmation message after copying. Snippet names from the twigl snippet library are now automatically protected from renaming, avoiding a naming conflict after inserting a snippet. The "Sound" toggle's accessibility label now states clearly that it refers to a separate program from the one shown, specific to twigl.app. ### Fixed Twigl.app exports in **ES 3.00** mode now use current texture functions (the old ones no longer compiled in a real browser). Multi-target (**MRT**) exports in ES 3.00 now include the layout information WebGL2 requires. The **Backbuffer** and **Sound** toggles in the Twigl export panel now genuinely update the live preview. The command palette's "Copy as twigl" action now always matches what's shown on screen (including in MRT mode). Restoring a session on launch now correctly reopens the document and tab that were active when the app was last closed. A document that was intentionally cleared (but not saved) is no longer replaced with the default shader on the next launch. The stats panel now correctly reports whether frequency-aware renaming actually ran on the last pass. Improved the performance of the frequency-aware renaming option used by "Golf harder".

item.title: MicroShader v4.0.0
item.description: Major release: Phase 34 (twigl.app export parity) and Phase 38 (UI overhaul with multi-document editing) are both externally visible, workflow-changing additions. ## Highlights **twigl.app export parity** (classic/geek/geeker/geekest modes, ES 300 rewriting, MRT/backbuffer naming, tweet-budget presets). **Neyret and Inigo Quilez idiom libraries** ("Golf Tips" panel) — opt-in, inert suggestions, never auto-applied. **"Golf harder" compression-aware search**, extended with a hand-written DEFLATE encoder and a simulated-annealing deep search mode. **UI overhaul**: tab strip regrouped into Author/Analyze/Export/Settings, a new always-visible document tab strip with multi-document editing, session persistence across restarts, one-click export presets, `.ushaderprofile` save/load, exclude-list import, PNG viewport capture, and self-contained HTML session reports. **Branding/licensing cleanup** and an **offline-first audit**: confirmed zero network calls at run time across every new module. See `CHANGELOG.md` for the full per-phase changelog.

item.title: MicroShader v3.0.2.0
item.description: # Changelog All notable changes to µShader are documented in this file. ## [v3.0.2.0] ### Added `golf.md` Phase 31.1 (`for`-loop header golfing) is now implemented: a new `rust-core/src/loop_golf.rs` module folds the common Shadertoy/demoscene idiom of a standalone float counter incremented at the top or bottom of a `for` loop body (`i++`, `i+=1.`, or `i=i+1.`, the latter proven via `expr.rs`'s `Expr` parser rather than raw-token matching) into the `for(...)` header itself, e.g. `float i=0.;for(int j=0;j<8;j++){i+=1.;...}` becomes `for(float i=0.;i++<8.;){...}`. The rewrite is skipped outright whenever the loop contains a `continue`, whenever the old loop variable is still read inside the body, or whenever the counter's final value is read anywhere after the loop (its scope narrows to the loop once hoisted into the header), matching this document's "decline rather than risk" precedent from Phase 30.4. `AggressiveOptions::loop_header_golf` (off by default, including in `Maximum`, consistent with Phase 30.1's own opt-in-only precedent for behavior-adjacent passes). Added `fixtures/loop_header_golf.glsl` (a raymarching loop and a fractal-iteration loop, the two most common Shadertoy loop shapes), Rust unit tests covering all three increment shapes plus every decline case, a `never_worsens_deflate_budget_on_the_tracked_fixture` regression test, and a new `tests/wgl_equivalence_test.cpp` block proving the fixture renders pixel-identically before and after the rewrite under the Phase 15 WGL equivalence harness. `golf.md` Phase 31.2 (`do`/`while` → `for` and `while` → `for` normalization) is now implemented in `rust-core/src/loop_golf.rs`: `golf_loop_forms` rewrites `while(cond){...}` to `for(;cond;){...}` (dropping the condition entirely for `while(true)`, since an empty `for` test clause means "always true") and folds a `do{S}while(cond);` loop into `for(;S,cond;);` via the comma operator whenever `S`'s statements are every one of them already representable as a bare `Expr` (reusing Phase 30.3's `classify_fusable_statement` whitelist) — both rewrites are unconditionally behavior-preserving, so unlike Phase 31.1 this pass carries no `continue`/read-after-loop safety check, only a size guard: it is skipped outright unless the rewritten header is strictly shorter in both raw character count and `budget.rs`'s estimated DEFLATE size, the same char/DEFLATE-size comparison Phase 30.1 already uses. New `AggressiveOptions::loop_form_golf` toggle (off by default, including in `Maximum`). Added `fixtures/loop_form_golf.glsl` (an unbounded `while(true){...break;}` raymarch loop and a fully-fusable accumulation `do`/`while` loop), Rust unit tests for both the `while`→`for` and `do`/`while`→`for` directions, a "no change when not shorter" test for a non-trivial `while` condition (where the `while(`/`for(;`..`;)` boilerplate ties exactly in character count), decline tests for a brace-free `while` body and for a `do`/`while` body containing a `break` or a declaration, and a `never_worsens_deflate_budget_on_the_tracked_fixture` regression test. `golf.md` Phase 31.3 (early-return / guard-clause ternary extension) is now implemented: `try_match_ternary` in `rust-core/src/aggressive.rs` is joined by a new `try_match_guard_clause_ternary`, widening `ternary_from_if_else` to also recognize the tail-of-function `if(cond){return a;}return b;` idiom (with or without braces around the `if` arm) and collapse it to `return(cond)?a:b;` — a strictly more constrained special case of the existing assignment-pair form (single trailing `return`, no `else` branch), not a new safety class. The guard-clause form is only recognized when the second `return` sits exactly at a function's closing `}`, reusing `callgraph.rs`'s existing `find_function_definitions` for that boundary check rather than inventing new function-boundary detection. No new toggle: the existing `AggressiveOptions::ternary_from_if_else` flag covers both forms. `fixtures/ternary_from_if_else.glsl` gained a third function (`clampSign`, now called from `mainImage` so it survives dead-function elimination) exercising the guard-clause case, and `rust-core/src/golfer.rs`'s existing ternary test block gained seven new unit tests: braced and unbraced guard-clause collapses, and decline cases for an `else` branch being present, the guard clause not being at the tail of the function, a non-`return` second arm, a multi-term arm, and confirmation that no dedicated toggle exists. Phase 35.1 and 35.2 (Fabrice Neyret idiom library) land as a new `rust-core/src/neyret.rs` module: a 10-entry short-rotation-matrix constant catalogue with `suggest_rotation_matrix_constants(source)` detection (matches `mat2(cos(a),sin(a),-sin(a),cos(a))`-style constructions with a provably compile-time-constant angle against the catalogue, within a 0.25° tolerance), and a 5-entry `fract(sin(dot(...)))`-family hash-snippet catalogue (`hash11`/`hash12`/`hash21`/`hash22`/`hash13`) distinct from twigl's `fsnoise`. This is intentionally backend-only: 35.3 and 35.4 are not started, since they depend respectively on `golf.md` Phase 30's comma-fusion pass and Phase 33's Golf Tips panel, and neither exists in this codebase yet. See `ROADMAP.md` Phase 35 for the full status note. Phase 34 (twigl.app golfing-mode parity) is now fully implemented. `rust-core` adds the `snoise2D`/`snoise3D`/`snoise4D` snippet entries (completing the documented 10-entry geekest-mode snippet library) and exposes the full Twigl export surface through a new `capi` FFI layer (`ushader_twigl_rewrite`, `ushader_twigl_rewrite_mrt`, `ushader_twigl_snippet`, `ushader_twigl_snippets_json`, `ushader_estimate_twigl_geekest_budget`, `ushader_twigl_export_uniform_names_json`). The C++ shell gains a new "Twigl" tab (`Win32TwiglExportPanel`) with the Classic/Geek/Geeker/ Geekest mode ladder, an ES 300 es toggle, MRT/backbuffer/sound toggles, one-click snippet-insert buttons (via a new `Win32TextEditor::insert_text_utf8` helper), a live preview, and a byte-budget badge, opened via a new rebindable `Ctrl+Alt+T` chord. `tests/wgl_equivalence_test.cpp` now also compiles/links the `twigl_classic.glsl` and `twigl_geekest.glsl` regression fixtures under the desktop GL WGL context; `twigl_300es.glsl` remains permanently excluded (documented ES300/desktop-GL-core incompatibility). See `ROADMAP.md` Phase 34 for full details. `golf.md` Phase 29 (frequency-aware renaming & swizzle-alphabet golf) is now fully implemented: - **29.1** — the opt-in, deterministic frequency-aware identifier-renaming heuristic evaluates a compression-aware alternative mapping against the existing rename order and only keeps it when the final post-pass DEFLATE estimate is strictly better; otherwise output stays on the historical mapping. `AggressiveOptions::frequency_aware_renaming` (default on in `Maximum`, off in `Safe`). Added `fixtures/frequency_renaming.glsl` and Rust regression coverage for determinism and no-regression budget checks. - **29.2** — swizzle-alphabet golf: a new `rust-core/src/swizzle.rs` module recolors every `.xyzw`/`.rgba`/`.stpq` swizzle access to whichever of the three interchangeable alphabets the caller selects, never touching struct member access. `Auto` mode tries all three against the DEFLATE estimator and keeps the smallest. Surfaced as a `swizzle_alphabet` combo in `golf_controls.cpp` / `win32_golf_controls.cpp`, persisted by a `.ushaderprofile` schema minor-version bump (backward compatible: an absent field defaults to `Auto`). Added `fixtures/swizzle_alphabet.glsl` and a new `tests/wgl_equivalence_test.cpp` block that compiles the fixture's `.xyzw` source against a hand-verified `.rgba` recoloring and proves they render pixel-identically under the Phase 15 WGL equivalence harness; the recoloring itself is golden-mastered by a new Rust test against the same fixture so the two can never drift. - **29.3** — non-constant swizzle/vector factoring: a new `factor_repeated_vector_args` pass in `aggressive.rs` generalizes `reduce_constant_vectors` to identical **pure identifier** arguments (`vec3(a,a,a)` -> `vec3(a)`, `vec3(p.x,p.x,p.x)` -> `vec3(p.x)`), never touching a not-all-equal or literal-only call (those remain the sole responsibility of `reduce_constant_vectors`, with no double-counting between the two stats). `AggressiveOptions::factor_repeated_vector_args` (default on). Added `fixtures/vector_argument_factoring.glsl` and four Rust unit tests. - The CLI (`golf`) now reports `vector args factored` and `swizzles recolored` in its human-readable summary and exposes `vector_args_factored`/`swizzles_recolored` as new JSON/CSV report columns, alongside the existing `--profile`/`.ushaderprofile` wiring for all three sub-phases. - See `ROADMAP.md` §6 and `golf.md` §5 for the full status note. Phase 30 (aggressive inlining & cross-statement subexpression golf) remains not started; its one landed-but-unfinished pass, `fuse_statement_sequences`, stays off by default until Phase 30 ships its own fixture, tests, and checkbox. `golf.md` Phase 30.3 (statement-sequence fusion via the comma operator) is now fully implemented. The `fuse_statement_sequences` pass already existed in `aggressive.rs`; this closes it out with `fixtures/statement_fusion.glsl`, five Rust regression tests (basic fusion, declaration/`if`-brace/`return` boundaries, off-by-default, and a DEFLATE never-worse check), a "Fuse statement sequences" checkbox in the Win32 Controls panel, and full `.ushaderprofile` persistence (`.ushaderprofile` schema bumped to version 3). The `Maximum` built-in profile now explicitly enables it and `Safe`/ `None` explicitly disable it, closing a latent gap where the pass silently stayed on in both via `GolfPassToggles`' own default. The shared `AggressiveOptions::all()`/`golf(source, true)` test helper deliberately still keeps it off, the same precedent already set for `frequency_aware_renaming`, since flipping it there would silently change the expected output of roughly a hundred pre-existing exact-string regression tests. Also backfills `factor_repeated_vector_args` and `swizzle_alphabet` (Phase 29.2/29.3) into `docs/ushaderprofile.schema.json` and `docs/ushaderprofile-schema.md`, which had been implemented in `golf_profile.cpp` but never documented. Phase 30.1 (aggressive multi-call-site inlining), 30.2 (whole-shader macro CSE), and 30.4 (declaration hoisting) remain not started. UX feedback fix: the Controls panel becomes a persistent right-side inspector instead of a full-screen tab, and two actions that were previously keyboard/command-palette-only get visible buttons. ### Changed The "Controls" tab is removed; `Win32GolfControls` now renders as a fixed-width (300px) inspector docked to the right edge, visible on every tab except Viewport (which keeps the full window width, needed for Compare mode's split render). All other tab content (editors, Diff, Trace, Stats, Appearance, About) narrows to make room; the Source/Golfed minimap repositions to stay left of the inspector instead of the raw window edge. The pass-checkbox list switched from two columns to one: the two-column layout was sized for a full-width tab and truncated labels like "Common subexpressions" once squeezed into the 300px inspector. Single column uses the inspector's full available height instead, with no truncation. ### Added A "Golf" button at the top of the inspector runs the same recompile action as `F5` or the command palette's "Run golf" entry — previously keyboard/palette-only. A "Formatted view" toggle button in the top-right of the Golfed tab's content area, mirroring the existing `Ctrl+Shift+F` chord — previously also keyboard/palette-only. Both new buttons (`src/ui/win32_tool_button.h/.cpp`, a small reusable owner-drawn button) are registered for UI Automation like every other Phase 26 control, verified live with the same `System.Windows.Automation` client used throughout that phase.

item.title: ShadertoyCameraPath v2.0.0
item.description: # Shadertoy Camera Path & Keyframe FX Timeline Studio — v2.0.0 "Ultimate Edition" This release ships the standalone Windows binary (`shadertoy-camera-path-studio.exe`) only. The Inno Setup installer (`.stcp` file association, Start Menu shortcut) is **not** attached to this release yet — it needs to be built on a machine with Inno Setup 6 installed, which this build environment doesn't have. Run the binary directly (portable mode); see README.md for details. Full per-phase changelog below. -- ## [2.0.0] — 2026-07-29 "Ultimate Edition" ### Added **Phase 16 — v2.0.0 "Ultimate Edition" Certification & Release:** - **16.1 Cross-phase regression:** `cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast` passes with zero failures across all five crates. New `slang-codegen/tests/glsl_slang_parity.rs` re-validates GLSL ⇄ Slang round-trip parity at the shared-IR/embedded-literal level (both backends are never actually compiled/executed in this environment — see the test's own doc comment for exactly what is and isn't claimed). Offline-isolation audit: confirmed no network-capable crate (`reqwest`/`hyper`/`tokio`/`ureq`/`tungstenite`/`curl`/TLS) appears anywhere in `Cargo.lock`; the one pre-existing caveat is the off-by-default `puffin-profiling` feature's local-only TCP listener, unchanged from Phase 14. Stress certification reuses Phase 14's existing 10k-keyframe stress-test generator/test rather than adding a new mechanism - **16.2 Documentation:** new `docs/user_guide.md` covering every panel added in Phases 7–15; new `docs/plugin_sdk.md` stating plainly that the plugin system is a design note, not a shipped feature; `docs/performance.md` gained a section pointing at the Phase 14 Diagnostics panel as the live complement to the static benchmarks. New in-app **Getting Started** panel (View menu) — an offline, paginated Next/Back/topic-list walkthrough, no video/network. Tooltips (`.on_hover_text`) added to every action button across all 14 panel files with interactive controls — Expression Graph (including one tooltip per node type in the node palette), Timeline, Curve Editor, FX Triggers, Diagnostics, Physics & Mocap, Multi-Camera, Asset Library, Layers/Sequences/Variants/History, Export/Preview, Preferences, 3D Viewport, and Code Export — roughly 98 tooltip sites, up from 12 across 3 files. `about.rs`/`getting_started.rs` (self-explanatory static content) and `menu_bar.rs` (egui menus don't reliably show hover tooltips while open, and labels are already descriptive) were deliberately left alone - **16.3 Final packaging:** `installer/setup.iss`'s `AppVersion` bumped to `2.0.0`; the new docs files are now included in the installed file set. No new bundled binaries exist to add (no `slangc`, no plugin samples) — offline-first isolation at installer level is unchanged from Phase 6 - **16.4 v2.0.0 release:** performed with explicit user authorization. Workspace version bumped to `2.0.0` across all crates; repository URL corrected (`ShadertoyCameraPath`, not the stale `Z-GL-Shadertoy` placeholder) in `Cargo.toml`, `README.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, and the in-app About tab; git repository initialized, reviewed for stray/sensitive files before staging (a personal test certificate, an old project zip backup, a Claude Code session lock file, and unrelated leftover Next.js scaffold files were excluded via `.gitignore`, not committed), single initial commit, pushed to `github.com/Patrickjaillet/ShadertoyCameraPath`, tagged `v2.0.0`, release binary built (`cargo build --release`), and published to GitHub Releases - Tests: 1 new cross-backend parity test **Phase 11 — Slang Language Compatibility Layer (Export & Import):** - New `slang-codegen` workspace crate, sharing `glsl-codegen`'s `TimelineIr`/`ChannelIr`/`KeyframeIr` directly rather than duplicating it. `KeyframeIr` gained optional `in_tangent`/`out_tangent` fields and `InterpolationKindIr` a `CubicBezier` variant (distinct from `Unsupported`) so the shared IR can carry Bezier control-point data — the GLSL backend's existing zero-fallback behavior for Bezier channels is unchanged, while Slang gets a real cubic-Bernstein template, closing that gap on the Slang side only - **11.1 Export pipeline:** `evaluateTimeline`-equivalent generation, per-channel accessors (`getFOV`, `getCameraPosition`, `getCameraRotation`, `getTrigger`, `getAudioEnvelope`), Catmull-Rom/B-Spline/SLERP/Cubic-Bezier templates in Slang/HLSL syntax (`float3`/`float4`, `lerp`, `atan2`, HLSL-style array initializers instead of GLSL's `T[N](...)` constructor call), `[shader("fragment")]`/`[shader("compute")]` entry-point stubs, a `SlangTargetProfile` enum (GLSL 450/ES 300, HLSL SM5/SM6, SPIR-V 1.5, Metal — profile choice recorded in the header comment only), Debug/Readable/Minified verbosity (reusing `glsl-codegen`'s minifier), and a `wrapMod` helper reproducing GLSL's floored-modulo `mod()` for `Cycle`/`PingPong` extrapolation (Slang/HLSL's `fmod` truncates toward zero and would wrap the wrong direction) - **11.2 Offline validation:** new `vendor_slangc.sh`/`.bat` scripts fetch the official prebuilt `slangc.exe` (`shader-slang/slang` v2026.14, Windows x86_64) into gitignored `vendor/slangc/` — never bundled into the shipped installer. `slang-codegen/tests/slangc_validation.rs` shells out to it and verifies the generated Slang really compiles for Glsl450/HlslSm5/HlslSm6/Spirv15/Metal, skipping gracefully on a machine that hasn't run the vendor script; CI fetches and caches it so this runs for real on every push. `entry::validator::validate_structural_balance` still runs as a fast additional syntax check in the golden-file tests. `SlangTargetProfile::known_gap()` for `GlslEs300` documents a real gap found while building this test: `slangc`'s CLI exposes no GLSL ES profile at all (only desktop `glsl_150`..`glsl_460`), so that one profile is excluded from the compile test - **11.3 Import:** a Rust-native parser (`slang_codegen::import`) for the documented subset this crate's own export produces (`NAME_TIMES[N]`/`NAME_VALUES[N]` array pairs), with per-channel error diagnostics for malformed/mismatched arrays and partial import. Every imported channel reconstructs as `Linear` interpolation regardless of the original mode — keyframe times/values round-trip exactly (verified by an export → import → export test), but the original basis-function template isn't recovered - **11.4 UI:** a single unified "Code Export" panel (`app/src/ui/code_export_panel.rs`, replacing the earlier separate `glsl_panel.rs`/`slang_panel.rs`) with a GLSL/Slang target toggle and one shared Debug/Readable/Minified verbosity dropdown — the first verbosity *control* in the UI at all; both prior panels had hardcoded Readable with no picker. "GLSL Export"/"Slang Export" menu entries and `Ctrl+4`/`Ctrl+0` shortcuts still work, each pre-selecting that target. "Import Slang…" is a button shown when the Slang target is selected. The "About" tab now reports the `slangc` version that validated the build (via `app/build.rs` shelling out to `vendor/slangc/bin/slangc.exe -v` at compile time, baked in as `env!("SLANGC_VALIDATION_VERSION")`), falling back to an explicit "not available" message when built without `slangc` vendored. Bug caught while wiring this up: `slangc -v` prints its version to stderr, not stdout — `build.rs` was written checking stderr first after confirming this directly, not assuming it - Tests: 39 new tests in `slang-codegen` (31 unit + 4 golden-file + 2 round-trip + 1 real `slangc` compile check + 1 GLSL⇄Slang parity check) **Phase 15 — Accessibility, Customization & Professional Input Devices:** - **15.1 Accessibility:** eframe's `"accesskit"` feature is enabled, giving every existing labeled widget an automatically-derived accessible name for screen readers with no per-widget app code. Keyboard-only navigation uses `egui`'s built-in Tab/Shift+Tab focus-cycling, extended by the new unified keybinding dispatch (see 15.2) so panel switches and transport commands also have a keyboard path. `theme::UiDensity` (Compact/Comfortable/Spacious) scales spacing/padding/interact-size on top of the White theme. `theme::TRACK_COLORS_COLORBLIND_SAFE` (Okabe-Ito palette) is a selectable alternative to the default track-color palette, wired into the Timeline track headers and Curve Editor curve lines - **15.2 Keybinding & Workflow Profiles:** new `app/src/keybindings.rs` (`BindableKey`/`KeyCombo`/`Action`/`KeyBindings`) replaces the previous hardcoded shortcut `if` blocks in `app.rs` with a remappable, persisted (JSON) action-dispatch table; `default_profile`/`blender_style_profile`/`adobe_style_profile` presets are selectable (not auto-applied). New `app/src/workspace_layout.rs` (`WorkspaceLayout`/`WorkspaceLayoutStore`) saves/restores named presets of active panel + Timeline/Curve Editor pan-zoom + 3D viewport camera state — honestly scoped to this app's single-active-panel architecture rather than a docking-layout system, since `egui_dock` is a listed but entirely unused dependency - **15.3 Professional Input Devices:** new `app/src/input_devices/midi.rs` (via `midir`) parses MIDI CC messages and maps them to app targets (default: CC1 mod-wheel scrubs the playhead); new `app/src/input_devices/gamepad.rs` (via `gilrs`) polls stick axes each frame to orbit/pan the 3D viewport camera, with deadzone handling. Both degrade gracefully with a status label when no device is connected. All CC-parsing, mapping, and stick-to-camera math is pure and hardware-independent, giving the `app` crate its first-ever unit test suite - **15.4 Multi-Monitor Support:** `StudioApp::show_floating_viewport` pops the 3D viewport out into a real OS-level `egui` viewport (draggable to any monitor), falling back to an embedded `egui::Window` on backends without multi-viewport support; a fullscreen toggle sends `ViewportCommand::Fullscreen(true)` to that floating viewport specifically. Per-monitor DPI scaling is automatic and native to `winit`/`egui-winit`; a manual `Preferences::dpi_scale_override` slider (`ctx.set_zoom_factor`) is layered on top for users who want a different scale than native - New "Preferences" panel (`app/src/ui/preferences_panel.rs`, View menu entry) exposes all of the above: density/palette toggles, keybinding grid with click-to-rebind, workspace layout save/apply/delete, MIDI/gamepad enable + status, floating-viewport + fullscreen + DPI-override controls - New dependencies: `midir`, `gilrs` (app crate only), plus eframe's `"accesskit"` feature - Tests: 23 new unit tests (keybinding matching/rebind/save-load, workspace layout upsert/find/remove/round-trip, MIDI CC parsing/mapping, gamepad deadzone/orbit math) **Phase 14 — Advanced Diagnostics, Profiling & Auto-Optimization:** - **14.1 Real-Time Performance HUD:** `profile_timeline_evaluation` times a real (wall-clock, if coarse at curve-evaluation timescales) evaluation pass over every non-muted track, reporting total duration, active keyframe count, and a per-track breakdown; `PerformanceHistory` is a session-scoped capped ring buffer with an offline CSV export. App: a "Perf HUD" viewport toggle overlays eval/frame time and keyframe count live; the Diagnostics panel shows the per-track cost table, a rolling frame-time graph, and "Export Session Log (CSV)". Note: there's no separately measurable "GPU frame time" in this architecture — the 3D viewport is CPU-painter-drawn, not a real wgpu render pass — so only CPU-side timings are reported, documented as such rather than fabricated - **14.2 Shader Complexity Analysis:** `estimate_instruction_count` is a documented text-level heuristic (statement/operator/call counts), not a real compiler-verified instruction count; `platform_tier_report` checks it against rough guideline thresholds for Mobile/Integrated-GPU/Desktop. `detect_optimization_suggestions` finds constant-folding no-ops (`* 1.0`, `+ 0.0`, …) and always-true/always-false `if` branches (with real brace-matching for safely removing dead `if (false)` blocks); `apply_with_diff` performs the byte-range replacements and returns a before/after preview for the one-click "Apply Suggested Optimizations" action. New module `glsl-codegen/src/analysis/` (`complexity.rs`, `suggestions.rs`) - **14.3 Curve Simplification & LOD:** `simplify_curve` runs an iterative (non-recursive, stack-overflow-safe) Douglas-Peucker pass over each keyframe's `(time, value)` or `(time, x, y, z)` point, preserving both timing and shape within a tolerance — exact when kept segments are evaluated with linear interpolation, documented as approximate for curved interpolation modes between kept keyframes. `LodPreset` (Desktop/Integrated GPU/Mobile) wraps built-in tolerance presets. New module `core-engine/src/curve_simplify.rs`. App: tolerance slider + live preview + per-preset buttons in the Diagnostics panel, applied to the selected curve via undo-tracked `FullSnapshot` - **14.4 Memory & Stability Profiling:** new optional `heap-profiling` Cargo feature (mirrors the existing `puffin-profiling` pattern) wires `dhat` as the global allocator and writes `dhat-heap.json` for offline inspection with the dhat viewer — opt-in, adds nothing to a normal build. A panic hook (`app/src/crash_report.rs`) writes a local, never-transmitted crash report (timestamp, panic location/message, backtrace) to the app data directory; the Diagnostics panel lists captured reports. `generate_stress_test_project` builds a synthetic multi-track, multi-thousand-keyframe timeline for stability testing, exposed both as a core-engine test fixture (asserts a 10k-keyframe evaluation pass completes without panicking within budget) and as a "Generate Stress-Test Project" Diagnostics panel action - New module `core-engine/src/diagnostics/` (`performance.rs`, `stress_test.rs`). App: new "Diagnostics" panel bringing all of the above together - Tests: 8 new performance/stress-test unit tests, 7 curve-simplification tests, 12 shader-analysis tests **Phase 4.3 — Tangent handle gizmos & multi-keyframe group manipulation:** the 3D viewport's translation gizmo now actually works — fixed a pre-existing bug where the picked axis was never stored, making the drag code unreachable. `ViewportState::active_gizmo_handle: Option<GizmoHandle>` is now set by hit-testing on drag-start (`Position(axis)`, `Group(axis)`, `InTangent`, `OutTangent`) and cleared on drag-stop. **12.3 Variants (A/B Takes):** `VariantStore`/`TimelineVariant` — full named snapshots of the current tracks kept alongside the master, non-destructively; `diff_tracks` compares two track lists by matching tracks on name and keyframes on id (added/removed/modified), shared by both variant-vs-master and snapshot-vs-snapshot diffing; `merge_keyframes_from_variant` selectively promotes individual keyframes from a variant into master - App: new "Layers / Sequences / Variants / History" panel — layer stack editor (add/reorder/blend-mode/opacity/solo/mute/lock/duplicate/merge-down), sub-sequence manager with drill-in/drill-out navigation (temporarily swaps the Timeline/Curve Editor panels onto the sub-sequence's own tracks, with an explicit save-or-discard on drill-out) and root/nested instance placement, variant creation/diff/apply/selective-merge, and snapshot creation/diff/restore-with-confirmation plus marker add/remove/jump-to-time - New module `core-engine/src/library/` (`preset.rs`, `fragment_io.rs`, `thumbnail.rs`), re-exported from the crate root - App: "Asset Library" panel — search, per-entry thumbnail + favorite/apply/delete, save the selected curve as a preset or the selected track as a template, export/import template fragments, favorites & recently-used quick-access strip. Library persists to `asset_library.json` in the app data directory, independent of any single project - Tests: `AssetLibrary` CRUD/search/favorites/MRU/round-trip, fragment save/load and rejection of non-fragment files, thumbnail pixel-buffer sizing and PNG signature **Phase 10.3 — Motion Capture Import:** - `RigidBodySolver`: mass/stiffness/damping spring-damper integrator (semi-implicit Euler, unconditionally stable) for camera spring/inertia behavior, with a `critical_damping` helper and optional max-speed clamp - `ObstacleVolume` (sphere/box) + `ObstacleSet`: user-defined keep-out volumes with a configurable clearance margin and signed-distance queries - `preview_collision_avoidance`: non-destructive per-sample suggestion that pushes path positions penetrating an obstacle's margin-inflated surface back outside it; `bake_collision_avoidance` commits an approved preview into curve keyframes - `min_distance_diagnostic`: samples a curve's clearance to the nearest obstacle over time, for a diagnostic graph overlay - New module `core-engine/src/camera/physics.rs` and `core-engine/src/camera/collision.rs`, re-exported from `camera` and the crate root - item.description: # Changelog All notable changes to GLConverter are documented in this file. The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). ## [1.0.0] - 2026-07-25 ### Added Official software screenshot (`docs/screenshot.png`) referenced from the `README.md`. ### Changed `README.md` finalized for the `v1.0.0` release: usage instructions, keyboard shortcuts, build/deployment steps, and copyright/contact information reviewed and brought up to date. Project marked stable: first public `v1.0.0` release, matching the `package.json` version. ## [0.9.0] - 2026-07-25 ### Added Full automated test suite (Vitest): unit tests for every golfing technique (dead code elimination, declaration merging, loop golfing, ternary/`&&` conditional golfing, native call shortcuts, variable renaming, operator simplification), unit tests for every de-golfing technique (conditional expansion, loop expansion, operator expansion, block normalization, descriptive renaming), unit tests for the equivalence validator, the parser, the language detector, the session history store, and the JS/WASM engine bridge, and interface integration tests exercising the mounted application (mode and direction toggles, rules panel, keyboard shortcuts, engine badge). GitHub Pages compatibility verification script (`npm run verify:pages`), run automatically at the end of every production build, checking that every emitted asset reference is relative. `npm test` now runs before the build step in the GitHub Actions deployment workflow. ### Changed The Three.js background scene and the engine benchmark module are now loaded on demand via dynamic `import()` instead of being bundled into the application's initial entry chunk. Production build output is now split into cacheable vendor chunks (Three.js, CodeMirror, the AST/golfing engine) instead of a single monolithic bundle, reducing the initial entry chunk from roughly 1 MB to about 36 kB and removing the Vite large-chunk warning. ## [0.8.0] - 2026-07-25 ### Added Global keyboard shortcuts, active anywhere in the application: `Alt+G` toggles Golf / De-golf, `Alt+M` toggles Minified / Justified, `Alt+C` copies the converted code, `Alt+E` opens Export, `Alt+H` opens History, `Alt+B` opens Benchmark, `Alt+R` opens Rules, `Alt+I` opens Import, and `Escape` closes any open panel. Every corresponding button now shows its shortcut in a tooltip. Keyboard-visible focus outline applied consistently across every interactive element, and `aria-expanded` / `aria-haspopup` states kept in sync on all dropdown-style panels for assistive technology. Reactive Three.js background transition: the point-field background now animates a brief pulse (speed, size, and opacity) on every conversion, and respects the operating system's reduced-motion preference by disabling the animation entirely when requested. ### Changed Refined responsive breakpoints for tablet and mobile viewports: the header and its controls now wrap cleanly, dropdown panels (History, Benchmark, Export, Rules) constrain themselves to the viewport width instead of overflowing on narrow screens, and the status bar and header actions reflow on small screens. ## [0.7.0] - 2026-07-25 ### Added Local file import: drag and drop a `.js` or `.txt` file onto the original editor panel, or use the new "Import" button to pick a file, to load its content for conversion. Export of the converted code as a downloadable `.js` or `.txt` file from the new "Export" menu in the converted panel. One-click "Copy" button to copy the converted code to the clipboard, with transient confirmation feedback. Session-local conversion history: every distinct edit to the original code is recorded (debounced) with its timestamp, direction, and compression ratio, browsable from the new "History" panel and restorable with a single click. The history is kept in memory only and is cleared on page reload. Undo / Redo controls for the original editor, exposed both as header buttons and through the existing keyboard shortcuts. ## [0.6.0] - 2026-07-25 ### Added Rust engine compiled to WebAssembly, providing a high-performance implementation of the whitespace-compaction pass and lexical token counting used by the minified output and status bar. Transparent engine bridge: the application attempts to load the compiled WASM engine on startup and automatically falls back to the existing JavaScript implementation when the WASM module has not been built or fails to load, with no change in behavior or output for the end user. "Engine" badge in the header indicating whether the active engine is WASM or the JS fallback. Integrated performance benchmark panel comparing the JS and WASM engines on the current source across a fixed number of iterations, with per-task timing bars and a computed speedup factor. `npm run build:wasm` script compiling the Rust engine with `wasm-pack`, wired into the production build and into the GitHub Actions deployment workflow. ## [0.5.0] - 2026-07-25 ### Added Reverse conversion (de-golfing): golfed code can now be converted back into structured, readable code. Restoration of readable variable names: identifiers are renamed according to their role (function names, parameters, loop counters, general values) instead of the original single-letter golfed names. Restoration of indentation and block structure: single-statement bodies are re-wrapped in blocks and the result is reformatted with clean indentation. Heuristic reconstruction of common golfed patterns: ternary and `&&`-shortcut conditionals are expanded back into `if`/`else` statements, countdown `for` loops are expanded back into ascending loops, and double-negation / falsy-literal boolean shortcuts are expanded back into their explicit form. Functional equivalence validation: after de-golfing, the reconstructed code is re-golfed and compared against a canonical signature of the original input to confirm the conversion is behavior-preserving, shown as an "Equivalence" status badge. Direction toggle in the interface to switch between "Golf" (structured to golfed) and "De-golf" (golfed to structured) conversion. ## [0.4.0] - 2026-07-25 ### Added Advanced loop golfing: counting `for` loops are rewritten as reverse countdown loops when the loop variable is unused in the body and the bound is safe to evaluate once, shortening the loop header. Ternary and conditional golfing: `if`/`else` statements are rewritten as conditional (ternary) expressions for matching `return` statements and matching assignments, and single-branch `if` statements using an expression are rewritten with the `&&` short-circuit shortcut. Native call golfing: known JavaScript golfing shortcuts are applied automatically, including `Boolean(x)` to `!!x`, `indexOf` presence checks to `includes`, `Array.prototype` to `[]`, and `.apply(null, x)` calls to spread syntax. Configurable golfing rules panel: each golfing technique (dead code elimination, declaration merging, loop golfing, ternary golfing, native call golfing, variable renaming, operator simplification) can be toggled on or off independently, with the converted output updating immediately. Character count display for both the original and converted code. Compression score, shown as a percentage of characters saved by the conversion. ## [0.3.0] - 2026-07-25 ### Added Golfing conversion pipeline applied to every conversion: minification, variable renaming, operator simplification, declaration merging, and dead code elimination. Minification engine: strips whitespace, newlines, and redundant semicolons from the converted output. Scope-aware variable renaming engine, assigning short identifiers (`a`, `b`, `c`, ...) while avoiding collisions with global references and reserved words. Operator simplification engine: converts increment/decrement patterns and compound arithmetic assignments to their shorter forms, and boolean literals to their shortest equivalent. Automatic merging of adjacent variable declarations of the same kind. Dead code elimination: removes unreachable statements, redundant pure expression statements, and literal `if` branches. Toggle button to switch the converted panel between "Minified" and "Justified" output modes. "Justified" mode: readable reformatting of the converted code with clean indentation. ## [0.2.0] - 2026-07-25 ### Added Dual-pane code editor built on CodeMirror 6 (Original / Converted). White theme applied to the code editors, matching the interface. Real-time synchronization: edits in the original pane automatically update the converted pane. Automatic source language detection, with JavaScript as the priority language. Source code tokenization and AST parsing powered by Acorn. Status bar showing detected language, token count, and character count. ## [0.1.0] - 2026-07-25 ### Added Initial project foundation with Vite and TypeScript. GitHub Pages compatible build configuration. Three.js background scene integrated into the interface. White theme baseline styling. Rust and WebAssembly engine skeleton for the future conversion engine. Initial `ConversionEngine` core module. Continuous deployment workflow to GitHub Pages. `LICENSE`, `README.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`.

Transparent engine bridge: the application attempts to load the compiled WASM engine on startup and automatically falls back to the existing JavaScript implementation when the WASM module has not been built or fails to load, with no change in behavior or output for the end user. "Engine" badge in the header indicating whether the active engine is WASM or the JS fallback. Restoration of readable variable names: identifiers are renamed according to their role (function names, parameters, loop counters, general values) instead of the original single-letter golfed names. Restoration of indentation and block structure: single-statement bodies are re-wrapped in blocks and the result is reformatted with clean indentation. Heuristic reconstruction of common golfed patterns: ternary and `&&`-shortcut conditionals are expanded back into `if`/`else` statements, countdown `for` loops are expanded back into ascending loops, and double-negation / falsy-literal boolean shortcuts are expanded back into their explicit form. Functional equivalence validation: after de-golfing, the reconstructed code is re-golfed and compared against a canonical signature of the original input to confirm the conversion is behavior-preserving, shown as an "Equivalence" status badge. Direction toggle in the interface to switch between "Golf" (structured to golfed) and "De-golf" (golfed to structured) conversion. ## [0.4.0] - 2026-07-25 ### Added Advanced loop golfing: counting `for` loops are rewritten as reverse countdown loops when the loop variable is unused in the body and the bound is safe to evaluate once, shortening the loop header. Ternary and conditional golfing: `if`/`else` statements are rewritten as conditional (ternary) expressions for matching `return` statements and matching assignments, and single-branch `if` statements using an expression are rewritten with the `&&` short-circuit shortcut. Native call golfing: known JavaScript golfing shortcuts are applied automatically, including `Boolean(x)` to `!!x`, `indexOf` presence checks to `includes`, `Array.prototype` to `[]`, and `.apply(null, x)` calls to spread syntax. item.description: All four post-1.0 backlog items, implemented and verified end to end. ## Added **Drag & drop** — dropping a folder from Windows Explorer onto the Source group sets it as the source directory and prefills the archive name from the folder name. **Password-protected archives** — an optional "Password-protect" checkbox and password field produce AES-256 encrypted `.zip` files via [SharpZipLib](https://github.com/icsharpcode/SharpZipLib) (`EncryptedArchiveWriter`/`EncryptedArchiveVerifier`), alongside the existing unencrypted Stored/Deflate path. **Command-line mode** — `ZipAll.exe --source <dir> --dest <dir> [options]` compresses headlessly, sharing the same core engine as the GUI, with `--help`, `--mode`, `--password`, repeatable `--exclude-file`/`--exclude-dir`, and `--quiet`. Running the exe with no arguments (or a single folder path) still opens the GUI. **Explorer "Send to" integration** — an optional installer task adds a `ZipAll` shortcut to the current user's Send To folder; launching the app with a single folder argument pre-fills that folder as the source in the GUI, so exclusions/password can still be reviewed before compressing. 6 additional unit tests (45 total) covering password round-trips, wrong-password rejection, exclusions, Stored mode, and confirming an unencrypted reader cannot read the encrypted content. ## Verification Manually verified end-to-end on real Windows hardware: installer rebuilt with the new `sendto` task, install/launch/uninstall cycle (including the Send To shortcut) confirmed clean, Send To launch confirmed via screenshot with the source pre-filled, CLI run from a real console with correct exit codes and output for plain and password-protected archives. ## Known limitations Tested on Windows 10 x64 only; Windows 11 and ARM64 remain unverified.

item.description: ZipAll's first stable release: a native Windows desktop app (C#/.NET, WinForms) that zips a folder, with exclusions, a custom archive name, and a choice of destination. ## Added `CONTRIBUTING.md`: contribution ground rules (C#/.NET/WinForms-only, English-only, no source comments, White theme only, Windows-only, BCL-only archive format, self-contained-only dependencies), PR checklist, and bug report template. `tests/ZipAll.Core.Tests`: xUnit unit test project (39 tests) covering `WildcardMatcher`, `ExclusionEngine`, `DirectoryWalker`, and `ArchiveWriter`/`ArchiveVerifier`, including empty folders, deeply nested trees, Unicode/special-character file names, and large flat trees. `tests/REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md`: manual regression checklist to run against a built installer before every release. A real application screenshot (`docs/screenshot.png`), now embedded in the README. ## Fixed Inno Setup script: a mis-escaped `AppId` GUID and a `[Files]` wildcard entry that excluded every file the self-contained publish produces, both of which broke the installer build. `ArchiveWriter.CreateArchiveAsync` read `ZipArchiveEntry.Length`/`CompressedLength` after writing each entry, but those properties always throw `InvalidOperationException` in `ZipArchiveMode.Create` — every archive containing at least one file was broken. Found while writing the new unit test suite; fixed by deriving byte counts from the known file length and the underlying zip stream's position delta instead. ## Changed Version stamp moved to `1.0.0` (`MAJOR` now `1`). Installer build and install/uninstall cycle verified end-to-end (silent install, launch, silent uninstall with no residual files). Self-contained `win-x86` build published and smoke-tested under WOW64. ## Known limitations Tested on Windows 10 x64 only; Windows 11 and ARM64 have not been verified (no such machine was available during development). item.title: MicroShader v3.0.0
item.description: *Breaking change**: µShader's UI framework is now native Win32 + Direct2D/DirectWrite/GDI+ + WGL-hosted OpenGL — Dear ImGui, SDL3, and the ImGuiColorTextEdit widget are fully removed from the build. `ushader.exe` is the Win32 shell built through Phases 22–26; the old SDL3/ImGui app is gone, not just superseded. This closes the Phase 22–27 migration arc. This release ships a deliberately smaller, curated feature set, not full parity with the retired app — see "Removed / not yet ported" below and `ROADMAP.md` Phase 28 for the tracked follow-up plan. ### Changed `CMakeLists.txt`: removed the `SDL3`, `imgui`, and `imguicolortextedit` `FetchContent` dependencies and library targets; links `user32`, `gdi32`, `gdiplus`, `d2d1`, `dwrite`, and `opengl32` directly (all in-box on every Windows 10/11 edition, including LTSC 2019 — no separate runtime to install). The former `ushader_win32_shell` CMake target is renamed `ushader`, reclaiming the name from the deleted SDL3 app; its subsystem changed from `/SUBSYSTEM:CONSOLE` (a development-time console window) to `/SUBSYSTEM:WINDOWS` — verified live that no console window appears. `theme_tokens.h`'s color constants moved off `ImVec4` (the one remaining header-level ImGui dependency the Win32 shell had picked up) onto a local `tokens::Color4` struct with the same field layout. `installer/ushader.iss`, `README.md`, and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` rewritten to describe the actual shipped shell and its real dependencies (previously: FFmpeg, `gif-h`, Inter/Lucide fonts — all removed, see below). ### Removed / not yet ported Six features from the retired ImGui app did not make it into the Win32 shell during Phase 26 and were deferred rather than bundled into this release — tracked in `ROADMAP.md` Phase 28, not silently dropped: Golfing profiles (`.ushaderprofile` save/load, `Maximum`/`Safe`/ `None` built-ins) — the CLI's `--profile` flag and the published schema are unaffected, this is only the GUI-side save/load UI. Multi-document workspace (multiple open shaders as separate tabs) and the session-restore-on-launch behavior that depended on it. One-click "Copy as Shadertoy / Bonzomatic / bare main()" clipboard exports. Importing a Shader Minifier–style exclude-name list. Self-contained HTML session report export. Viewport capture/recording: PNG screenshots, and GIF/MP4/WebM recording (the latter bundled `ffmpeg.exe` and `gif-h`, both now removed along with the feature). ### Fixed `assets/fonts/` (`Inter.ttf`, `lucide.ttf`) removed — unused once the ImGui shell that loaded them was gone; this phase's own opening sentence explicitly named the Lucide font as something that must not survive it. Several latent build issues surfaced only once SDL3/ImGui's incidental include-path and link propagation went away: `exclude_list_import_test` needed a real source swap (`file_dialog_sdl.cpp` → `file_dialog.cpp`, and `import_exclude_list_action` changed from taking `SDL_Window*` to `HWND`), three test targets had a dead `SDL3::SDL3` link, and `ushaderprofile_schema_test` was missing an explicit `rust_core` link it had never needed before. `workspace.h`/`.cpp` and `golf_controls.h` had a transitive dependency on the deleted `theme.h`, decoupled with a local literal default and by dropping dead SDL-specific declarations. `scripts/check_contrast.py`'s token-parsing regex updated for the `ImVec4` → `Color4` rename — re-verified all four text/background pairs still pass WCAG AA (5.87:1 to 13.36:1). ### Known gap The Windows 10 LTSC 2019 hardware/VM acceptance pass from `ROADMAP.md` Phase 27 has not been performed — this development environment has no LTSC 2019 target. Everything verifiable here (clean build, all 8 test executables passing, `wgl_equivalence_test` still 5/5 bit-exact, live UI smoke test) is done.

item.title: MicroShader v1.2.5
item.description: ## New golf pass: common subexpression elimination When two declarations in a row initialize with a token-identical pure expression, the later ones now reference the first variable instead of recomputing it, e.g. `float a=dot(p,p),b=dot(p,p);` becomes `float a=dot(p,p),b=a;`. Deliberately scoped narrow for safety: only whole declaration initializers, only pure builtins/constructors (never a user function), and the candidate cache is cleared on every block boundary and any non-matching statement. Two real bugs were found and fixed during development, both now covered by regression tests: A variable-name lookup that read the pre-rename identifier instead of the actual rendered name. A cache-invalidation check that missed a brace following `)` or `else` rather than `;`. New "Common subexpressions" toggle in the Passes panel, matching per-pass counter in the stats panel. item.title: MicroShader v1.2.1
item.description: ## Phase 10: dark UI/UX overhaul Full replacement of the white theme with a dark, Adobe Premiere Pro-style editing workspace: Named color-token table backing every UI color. Compact chrome: 2px corner radius, flat accent-underlined tabs, thin scrollbars. Custom borderless window frame with its own title bar (icon, minimize/maximize/close). Dark text-editor palette for Source/Golfed panels. Viewport restyled as a Program Monitor: black letterboxing, compile-status dot, timecode readout. Icons now shift color between idle/hover/active states. About popup rebuilt as a dark card. New design references under docs/design/, WCAG AA contrast-checked. Also fixes a crash when minimizing the window (found and fixed during verification of this release). Unsigned installer - Windows SmartScreen may show an "unknown publisher" warning; click "More info" -> "Run anyway". Verified on Windows 10 (LTSC 2019, build 17763); not independently verified on Windows 11.

item.title: MicroShader v1.0.0
item.description: First stable release of uShader, a native Windows 10/11 GLSL shader golfer. ## Highlights Golfing engine: identifier renaming, numeric literal shortening, and whitespace stripping always run; an aggressive mode adds 14 further transformation passes (dead-code elimination, constant folding, declaration merging, function inlining, and more), each individually toggleable, plus a protected-names list. Live viewport with the standard Shadertoy uniform set (`iTime`, `iResolution`, `iMouse`, `iDate`, `iFrame`, `iFrameRate`), and a Compare mode that renders the source and golfed shaders side by side. GLSL-aware text editor with syntax highlighting and error-line highlighting on compile failure, plus a "Formatted view" toggle for the golfed output. Reduction stats: char/byte counts, reduction percentage, per-pass counters, and size-budget badges. Import/export: open and save `.glsl` files, copy the golfed output, export in Shadertoy format, and capture the viewport to PNG. About panel with logo, copyright, and links. ## Installing Download `uShader-Setup-1.0.0.9.exe` below and run it. The installer is unsigned (no code-signing certificate available), so Windows SmartScreen may show an "unknown publisher" warning — click "More info" -> "Run anyway". Requires Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit). Verified on Windows 10 (LTSC 2019, build 17763); not yet independently verified on Windows 11. See [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Patrickjaillet/MicroShader/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for the full per-phase history.
